hypotheses.paper: 1°, second sentence: P n'est autre que l'image réciproque par φ̃ de l'ensemble des points de H̊ où z < 1
hypotheses.note: Proved in its component form (poche_eq_connectedComponentIn: P is the connected component of each of its points in φ̃⁻¹(D)), and in the full form for the constant cote (poche_eq_preimage_of_cote_eq_zero). For a non-constant cote the full form is reduced to the connectedness of D ∩ φ̃(V) (poche_eq_preimage_iff, premierPrinted_iff) and not proved. See findings.

hypotheses.paper: proof a: « une application φ̃ de V sur S(n) … dont le germe en tout point de V appartient à J(V) »
hypotheses.note: exists_isDeveloping_eqOn_poche: IsDeveloping (GSR n) p (every jet in J(V), Ch. 1 Prop. 2's notion) and EqOn p φ P. « sur » read « dans » (questions).

hypotheses.paper: proof b: φ̃ est un homéomorphisme global (injective)
hypotheses.note: injective_of_isDeveloping_of_poche, stated for EVERY developing map of V, which is stronger and is how OQ-46's alternative reading is answered.

findings: 1°c, the full form (statement l.523–524; proof l.585–590), not proved for a non-constant cote and not refuted. The proof says at l.588 « on peut construire dans D ∩ φ̃(V) une ligne brisée allant de φ̃(M) à φ̃(N) ». That presumes D ∩ φ̃(V) connected, which the paper does not prove. The forward reference after the examples (l.184–186) claims only that P « n'est autre qu'une composante connexe de l'image réciproque ». Proved here: (i) the component form, for the developing map φ̃ and every point of P (poche_eq_connectedComponentIn), using condition b and a convex neighbourhood in H̊; (ii) the full form is exactly the connectedness the proof presumes, both for one V (poche_eq_preimage_iff: P = φ̃⁻¹(D ∩ φ̃(V)) ↔ IsPreconnected (D ∩ φ̃(V))) and for the printed statement (premierPrinted_iff: PremierPrinted n ↔ ConnexePrinted n); (iii) the full form holds for the constant cote z ≡ 0, where P = V (poche_eq_preimage_of_cote_eq_zero). The open case is therefore a non-constant cote, the case OQ-61 (a) would keep. No counterexample was found or formalised. Argued, not formalised: the planar examples tried all satisfy the full form, namely complements of a closed quadrant and unions of octant triangles of S(2) under the diagonal group, and convex domains. They either admit only the constant cote or are convex.

1°c, the inclusion P ⊆ φ̃⁻¹(D), which the proof (l.585–590) does not argue, needs z < 1 on φ(P). Condition a of Déf. 1′ (l.137–138) gives only « majorée par 1 ». It holds because φ(P) is open and an affine function reaching its supremum 1 at an interior point is constant, against inf z = 0 (IsPocheProj.cote_lt_one). Statement unaffected.

1°b, the bracket of l.568–570 (proof level, statement unaffected): « puisque GS(n, R) opère transitivement sur la fibre des jets de même source, il existe γ transformant φ̃ en la section φ̃ ∘ g ». Transitivity on fibres gives a γ at each point only. One γ for all of V needs V connected and the rigidity of GS(n, R) (Ch. 1 Prop. 2's uniqueness, IsDeveloping.existsUnique_smul_eq). Both are available, but the bracket names neither.

1°a (l.545–556), proof level, statement unaffected. The paper shows that a path of J(V) over a loop is closed (chemin_jets_ferme here) and concludes « L'assertation a en résulte immédiatement ». That step is the lifting criterion through the covering J(V) → V, for V connected and locally path connected. It is formalised with Mathlib's IsLocalHomeomorph.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts. Over P the paper composes each jet with g⁻¹. The formalisation reads the lift in the single chart φ ∘ g, whose source g⁻¹P contains both paths by Prop. 7 (jetSMul_eq_of_path). The argument is the same.

OQ-46, bearing only, deciding nothing. In the Theorem's situation (V connected, sweepable, with one pocket) every developing map of V is injective (injective_of_isDeveloping_of_poche). So the projective example of § 1 (l.172–179) holds there as printed, without « p injective sur P » (exemple_poche_projective_of_poche). The forward reference « on est toujours dans la situation considérée en exemple » (l.183–184) holds too (situation_exemple: P is a component of φ̃⁻¹(D), inf z = 0 on φ̃(P), and φ̃ maps segments from P into H̊). The examples themselves are about an arbitrary étalé W, which need not be sweepable, so OQ-46's counterexample to the printed examples is untouched.
questions: 1°'s second sentence (l.523–524, « P n'est autre que l'image réciproque par φ̃ de l'ensemble des points de H̊ où z < 1 », and l.586 « P = φ̃⁻¹(D ∩ φ̃(V)) ») against the forward reference (l.184–186, « P n'est autre qu'une composante connexe de l'image réciproque »). Reading taken: the component form is proved as the formalisation's claim (PremierComposantePrinted n, proved for every n). The printed full form is stated as PremierPrinted n, and premierPrinted_iff proves it equivalent to ConnexePrinted n. It is proved for z ≡ 0 and open otherwise. Neither reading has been made the formalisation of record; that is the author's decision.

OQ-46 (open). As the dispatch asked, 1°b is stated for every developing map of V (injective_of_isDeveloping_of_poche) and not only for the φ̃ of 1°a. exemple_poche_projective_of_poche then gives the one-to-one case of the examples that the Théorème shows always holds. This answers OQ-46's alternative reading within the Theorem's hypotheses. It does not rule between adding « p injective sur P » to the examples and that reading.

« une application φ̃ de V sur S(n) » (l.538) and « L'application définie en a de V sur S(n) » (l.559): « sur » is read « dans » (into). The onto reading is false: in the model, φ̃(V) is the open hemisphere H₀ ≠ S(n) (theoreme_premier_model), and 1° itself says « sur un ouvert de S(n) ».

kb_proposals: Lifting through J(V) without simple connectivity (Chapter2/Developpement.lean). Use Mathlib's IsLocalHomeomorph.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts, applied to the identity of V, with isCoveringMap_jets_proj and exists_path_lifts for existence. For the uniqueness condition, a path of J(V) over the source of one maximal-atlas chart ψ is the translate of ψ's jets by the sheet of its first point, by IsCoveringMap.eq_of_comp_eq on I (jetSMul_eq_of_path). Prop. 7 puts both paths into the source of the one chart φ ∘ g.

The chart φ ∘ g of a pocket chart and an automorphism is IsCompatibleChart.trans_aut (Chapter2/Mesure.lean). Its source g⁻¹P: from g • x ∈ P, `simpa [GXAut.smul_def, hP.source_eq]`. A developing map composed with g is developing via `isDeveloping_iff_isGXMorphism.2 ((isDeveloping_iff_isGXMorphism.1 hp).comp g.isGXMorphism)`.

Convex neighbourhoods in an open hemisphere: exists_isOpen_closedSeg_subset (a ball pulled back by an affine equivalence from nonempty_hemi_affineEquiv, through isOpenEmbedding_coe_affineEquiv, coe_image_affineSegment and affineSegment_image). Every point of S(n) lies in some open hemisphere: exists_mem_openHemisphere. With isProjSegment_of_chart they turn « a point adherent to P » into a segment of V from a point of P.

The cote is < 1 on a pocket: IsPocheProj.cote_lt_one, the maximum twin of cote_pos_of_ne_zero. A pocket's closure lies over H̊ (closure_poche_subset_preimage_hemisphere), and for z ≡ 0 the pocket is all of V (poche_eq_preimage_of_cote_eq_zero).
After `obtain ⟨φ', hφ', hs, ht, he⟩ := exists_chart_of_injective hp hinj`, run `subst he`. The developing map then becomes ⇑φ' everywhere, and condition b applies with ψ := φ'.

A non-degenerate sweepable witness with a non-constant cote and P ≠ V: theoreme_premier_demiDroite (]0, ∞[ ⊂ ℝ¹, canonical projective structure, P = ]0, 1[). Homotheties are GXAut through Sphere.hemiChart_apply_eq_smul with (LinearEquiv.smulOfNeZero ℝ _ c hc).toAffineEquiv and GXAut.ofBijective. The z ≡ 0 model of ℝⁿ is isBalayable_model / theoreme_premier_model.
